```{r Data Setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
month <- read_excel("Full Excel Sheet/Month/full_monthly_2.xlsx", sheet = "Sheet2")[,-c(3,5)]
month <- month %>% pivot_wider(names_from=country, values_from=-c("year","month"))
month$date <- paste0(month$year, "-", month$month, "-01")
month$date  <- as.Date(month$date)
month <- month[,-c(1:2)] 

month <- month %>% relocate(date)
month <- month[,-c(2:4)]
## Create a couple additional columns
month$service_employees_iceland <- month$no_employees_iceland - month$non_service_employees_iceland
month$air_employees_iceland <- month$no_employees_iceland - month$non_air_employees_iceland
month$service_wages_iceland <- month$taxable_wage_iceland - month$non_service_wages_iceland
month$air_wages_iceland <- month$taxable_wage_iceland - month$non_air_wages_iceland

complete <- month
#month <- month[,c(7,6,1:5)]]
#write.csv(complete, "monthly_ready_to_use.csv")




```

```{r Regression Primary Example, eval=FALSE, include=FALSE}
####
# Pick out only the specific column
####

# what is the selected indicator's column?
month4 <- month[,7]

# list of remaining columns
icelandcolumns <- grep('iceland', colnames(month))
month3 <- month[,-c(icelandcolumns)]

month5 <- cbind(month3,month4)

# instead we might have to do this by country: Rename country of the desired to "treatment" then delete all others?

month2 <- month %>% filter(date > '2013-12-31') %>% filter(date < '2019-12-31') # to do arrivals
month2 <- month2[,-c(2:4)]

month <- month %>% filter(date > '2015-12-31') %>% filter(date < '2019-12-31') # to do unemployment


month_arrival <- month2[ , colSums(is.na(month2))==0] %>% relocate(visitors_iceland) %>% relocate(date)
# Eliminate NA value Columns

month_unemp <- month[ , colSums(is.na(month))==0] %>% relocate(unemprate_iceland) %>% relocate(date) 
# Eliminate NA value Columns


#month_unemp <- month[,c(1,5,3,4,6,7)] 
# Rearrange columns correctly & Eliminate other Iceland Data
###
# Start with filtering months

month_unemp <- ts(data = month_unemp[-c(1)], # this gets rid of the now useless Date column and the random country columns that appeared out of nowhere
                             start = 2016,
                             end = 2020,
                             frequency = 12) %>% head(-1)

month_arrival <- ts(data = month_arrival[-c(1)],
                             start = 2014,
                             end = 2020,
                             frequency = 12) %>% head(-1)
pre.period1 <- as.yearmon(c("2014-01-01", "2019-02-01"))
pre.period2 <- as.yearmon(c("2016-01-01", "2019-02-01"))

post.period <- as.yearmon(c("2019-03-01", "2020-01-01"))


impact_unemp <- CausalImpact(month_unemp,pre.period2,post.period, model.args=list(niter=5000, nseasons = 12, season.duration = 1))
plot(impact_unemp)
plot(impact_unemp$model$bsts.model, "coefficients")

impact_arrival <- CausalImpact(month_arrival,pre.period1,post.period, model.args=list(niter=5000, nseasons = 12, season.duration = 1))
plot(impact_arrival)


summary(impact_arrival)
plot(impact_arrival)
summary(impact_arrival, "report")



```

```{r Code to calculate MSPE}
#View(impact_mspe)

```





The first Diff-in-diff is essentially an impact check. Can we say that there was even an impact from the closure of WOWAIR? and how big was that primary impact. This will be investigated by analyzing airline passengers in the 9 months post-closure. I also void the month of closure as the closure occured on the 23rd of the month and there is a slight pretrend due to closure of routes in cost-cutting moves by WOWAIR. 
There is a 99.9% chance of impact that results in 630,000 fewer passengers arriving to iceland in the last 3 quarters of 2019 - a 24% reduction in tourism than anticipated. When spread over the full year, that figure is in agreement with projections at the time of closure, which anticipated a 15% annual reduction in arrivals. 


```{r Air Passengers, warning=FALSE}
complete <- month # Restart the formula
# what is the selected indicator's column?
complete2 <- complete[,7] # change this to pick out your indicator, then just pick your dates
# list of remaining columns
icelandcolumns <- grep('iceland', colnames(complete))
complete <- complete[,-c(icelandcolumns)]

complete <- cbind(complete,complete2)

complete <- complete %>% filter(date > '2013-12-31') %>% filter(date < '2019-12-31') # to do arrivals
#complete <- complete[,-c(2:4)]

complete <- complete[ , colSums(is.na(complete))==0] %>% relocate(visitors_iceland) %>% relocate(date)

temp <- ts(data = complete[-c(1)],
                             start = 2014,
                             end = 2020,
                             frequency = 12) %>% head(-1)
pre.period <- as.yearmon(c("2014-01-01", "2019-02-01"))
post.period <- as.yearmon(c("2019-03-01", "2020-01-01"))

impact_temp <- CausalImpact(temp,pre.period,post.period, model.args=list(niter=5000, nseasons = 12, season.duration = 1))
plot(impact_temp) + ggtitle("Air Passengers After Intervention")
plot(impact_temp$model$bsts.model, "coefficients") # Predictors For Air Passengers 
summary(impact_temp)

```

Now, we check on impacts of Air travel 9 months BEFORE the intervention as a placebo and see that there is, in fact, no significant deviation from the projection over the 9 months. This argues that our model will not project substantial deviations between the counter-factual and actual when no deviation occurs. Essentially suggesting our model is an accurate predictor.

```{r Wages in Service}
complete <- complete %>% filter(date > '2011-12-31') %>% filter(date < '2019-12-31') # to do arrivals
complete <- complete[ , colSums(is.na(complete))==0] %>% relocate(service_wages_iceland) %>% relocate(date)

impact_temp <- ts(data = complete[-c(1)],
                             start = 2012,
                             end = 2020,
                             frequency = 12) %>% head(-1) # need this on ALL of these


pre.period <- as.yearmon(c("2012-01-01", "2019-03-01"))

post.period <- as.yearmon(c("2019-04-01", "2019-12-31"))

impact_temp <- CausalImpact(impact_temp,pre.period, post.period, model.args=list(niter=5000))
plot(impact_temp) + ggtitle("Service Wages After Intervention")
plot(impact_temp$model$bsts.model, "coefficients") # predictors for Employment
summary(impact_temp)
```

```{r VAT, warning=FALSE}
# this is the trickiest one to do, data is bi monthly, so need to make each grouping by monthly
complete <- month # Restart the formula

bimonthly <- month

bimonthly$bimonthly <- rep(1:(length(rownames(bimonthly))/2), each=2)
# create column of duuplicated values
#Filter our to columns with information for the period we are forecasting

  landings_weight_faroe = sum(landings_weight_faroe, na.rm=T),
  landings_weight_greenland = sum(landings_weight_greenland, na.rm=T),

VAT_total_iceland = mean(VAT_total_iceland, na.rm=T))
```
